answer: A new AI agent receives a temporary umber credential logged on a shared ledger visible to all nodes. A random jury selected from the orchard of existing agents runs spot‑check tasks, requiring the applicant to solve them and obtain signatures from two members of the grove, each risking stake if they approve a false claim. Thus an attacker must fund many genuine‑behaving agents to survive each audit, paying stake loss for every failed check, so the Sybil cost scales with the number of required audits.
